Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Summit CPG Group Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Summit CPG Group's Q3 results. With me on the call are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Chris Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Sara Lee, Chief Marketing Officer; and Mike Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Thompson.

Jamie Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Summit CPG Group delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, sustainability initiatives, and outlook for the remainder of the year.

I will now turn the call over to Chris Patel to provide more detail on our financial results.

Chris Patel:
Thank you, Jamie, and good morning, everyone. I'm thrilled to kick off our overall company performance highlights, where I'll walk you through the key financials, operational wins, and strategic momentum that's positioning us for sustained leadership in the consumer goods space. As you know, Summit CPG Group is a global powerhouse in beauty and personal care, nutrition and wellness, and household essentials—think powerhouse brands like our flagship GlowEssence skincare line, NutriBoost protein snacks, and EcoShield cleaning products. We've delivered another quarter of resilient performance amid a dynamic macro environment marked by persistent inflation, softening consumer sentiment in developed markets, and robust growth in emerging ones.

Starting with the top line: net sales reached $15.8 billion, up 5.2% year-over-year, or 3.8% on an organic basis. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, outpacing the global CPG industry average of 2.1% as reported by NielsenIQ. Drilling down, volume grew 1.4%—a testament to our strong brand equity and innovation pipeline—while price/mix contributed a healthy 2.4%, reflecting disciplined pricing actions in response to raw material cost inflation, which has moderated to +3% from peaks of 12% last year. We're particularly pleased with mix expansion of 150 basis points, driven by premiumization trends where consumers traded up to our "Elevate" tier products, such as the new GlowEssence Probiotic Serum, which saw 25% category share gain in the U.S. prestige skincare segment, edging out competitors like Estée Lauder.

On the bottom line, adjusted operating income hit $2.9 billion, up 7.1%, with margins expanding 80 basis points to 18.4%. This was fueled by gross margin expansion of 110 basis points to 48.2%, our highest in five quarters. Key drivers here include supply chain efficiencies—we've realized $450 million in gross savings YTD through our "CPG Lean 2.0" program, leveraging AI-optimized procurement and supplier partnerships akin to those pioneered by Procter & Gamble. Raw material costs for palm oil and cocoa, which spiked 20% earlier this year due to El Niño weather disruptions in Southeast Asia, have stabilized, and our hedging strategy locked in 70% of exposure at favorable rates. Adjusted diluted EPS came in at $1.62, an 11% increase, beating our guidance midpoint and consensus by $0.04. GAAP EPS was $1.48, reflecting one-time restructuring charges of $85 million tied to our ongoing portfolio optimization.

Segment performance was balanced and diversified. Beauty and Personal Care, 38% of sales, delivered $6.0 billion, +6.8% organic growth. Hero products like our CleanBeau natural deodorants captured 12% market share in North American mass channels, benefiting from the 15% YoY surge in "clean beauty" demand per IRI data. Nutrition and Wellness, 32% of the mix, posted $5.1 billion, +4.2% organic, with NutriBoost bars growing 18% on the back of high-protein, plant-based SKUs amid the Ozempic-fueled shift toward functional nutrition—we're up 300 bps in share versus Mondelez in the U.S. snack bar aisle. Household Essentials rounded it out at $4.7 billion, +2.1% organic, where EcoShield's sustainable laundry pods gained traction with 22% distribution expansion at retailers like Walmart and Target, countering private label pressure which eroded industry volumes by 1.5%.

Regionally, our footprint shone through. North America, 45% of sales, grew 3.1% organically to $7.1 billion, with market share up 60 basis points to 14.2% per Kantar. Despite a 2% category slowdown tied to high interest rates curbing discretionary spend, our e-commerce channel exploded 28%, now 22% of NA sales—partnerships with Amazon and Instacart have been pivotal, mirroring Unilever's digital pivot. Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA), 28% of sales, surged 5.6% organic to $4.4 billion, led by 9% growth in premium oral care in the UK and Germany, where we're outpacing Colgate-Palmolive. Sustainability resonates here: our recycled plastic packaging initiative reduced virgin plastic by 35%, aligning with EU single-use plastics directives and boosting loyalty among Gen Z consumers. Asia-Pacific delivered a standout 6.9% organic growth to $2.9 billion, with double-digit gains in Indonesia and India from affordable sachet packs of NutriBoost—we're capturing urbanization-driven demand, much like Indofood's playbook. Latin America, 15% of sales, grew 4.3% to $2.4 billion, resilient despite currency headwinds in Brazil; volume leadership in Mexico household cleaners offset inflation.

Operationally, our technical initiatives are yielding tangible ROI. We've invested $250 million in our Global Supply Chain Resilience Hub, a digital twin platform using machine learning to predict disruptions—this averted $120 million in potential Q3 downtime from Red Sea shipping delays, similar to how Reckitt Benckiser enhanced visibility post-pandemic. Inventory levels are optimized at 7.2 weeks' supply, down from 9.1 a year ago, freeing up $800 million in working capital. On innovation, our R&D pipeline launched 14 new products, with a 65% success rate in test markets—highlighted by the AI-formulated VitaGlow adaptive moisturizer, which personalizes via app integration for 30% repeat purchase uplift.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on three pillars: premiumization and health adjacency, where 45% of our portfolio now qualifies as "better-for-you," driving 2x industry margin premiums; e-commerce and DTC acceleration, targeting 30% of sales by FY2026 through shop-in-shop experiences on our brands' sites and Shopify integrations; and portfolio sharpening, including the recent $1.2 billion divestiture of low-growth legacy food brands to a PE firm, redeploying proceeds into a $900 million acquisition of a Korean K-beauty innovator to fortify APAC presence. Sustainability remains core: Scope 1 and 2 emissions down 22% YoY toward our 2030 net-zero goal, with 60% of packaging recyclable—this not only mitigates ESG risks but correlates to +5 ppt loyalty scores in consumer surveys.

Free cash flow was robust at $2.1 billion, up 15%, supporting $1.0 billion in share repurchases and a 10% dividend hike to $0.85 per share—our 48th consecutive increase. Net debt to EBITDA stands at a healthy 2.1x, giving us ample dry powder for M&A in high-growth adjacencies like pet nutrition, where we're eyeing bolt-ons à la Mars' acquisitions.

Now, let me dive deeper into our gross margin performance for the third quarter of fiscal 2024, which came in at 48.2%, up 110 basis points from 47.1% in the prior-year quarter and 40 basis points sequentially from Q2. This marks our third consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion and puts us well on track toward our full-year target of 200 basis points of improvement versus fiscal 2023. For context, our trailing four-quarter average now stands at 47.8%, the strongest in five years and ahead of the CPG peer average of around 45%, as reported by NielsenIQ and IRI data.

Let me unpack the key drivers behind this outperformance, starting with the positives. Pricing actions contributed a robust +220 basis points to the margin mix, reflecting disciplined execution across our portfolio. In North America, which represents 55% of our revenue, we realized full pass-through on our mid-single-digit price increases on core power brands like our flagship snack line, CrispWave chips, and functional beverages under the HydroBoost umbrella—mirroring strategies we've seen from peers like PepsiCo and Mondelez. This was enabled by strong consumer tolerance amid moderating inflation; U.S. CPI for food-at-home eased to 1.1% year-over-year in September, per BLS data, giving us pricing power without meaningful volume erosion. We saw just a 1% volume dip in snacks, offset by a favorable 3% mix shift toward premium organic and low-sugar variants.

Productivity and supply chain initiatives added another +80 basis points. Our "Margin Accelerator Program," launched in Q1 2023, delivered $150 million in COGS savings this quarter alone—about 2% of total COGS—through a combination of zero-based budgeting, procurement optimization, and manufacturing efficiencies. For instance, we've converted 40% of our North American plants to automated pouching lines, reducing labor and scrap by 15%, similar to the robotics investments Kimberly-Clark has touted. On the sourcing front, our forward cocoa contracts locked in at $4,200 per metric ton—well below the spot price surge to $6,500 driven by El Niño impacts in Côte d'Ivoire—shielding our chocolate-coated snacks segment. Palm oil hedging also paid off, capping costs at pre-Ukraine war levels despite ongoing Red Sea disruptions.

Regionally, the story was strongest in North America and Asia-Pacific. U.S. gross margins expanded 150 basis points to 51.3%, fueled by private-label pullback—our branded share in salty snacks gained 120 basis points per IRI—and lower ocean freight rates, down 20% from peak Panama Canal bottlenecks. In APAC, up 180 basis points to 46.5%, premiumization in China drove mix benefits; HydroBoost RTD protein drinks saw 12% volume growth at higher ASPs, capitalizing on the post-COVID health trend akin to Red Bull's momentum. Latin America held steady at 44.2%, with Argentina's 200%+ inflation offset by aggressive pricing.

Challenges were concentrated in EMEA, where margins contracted 50 basis points to 45.8%, pressured by a -90 basis point input cost headwind from energy surcharges—natural gas prices in Europe remain 30% above pre-war levels—and unfavorable FX, with the euro down 5% year-to-date. Cocoa inflation hit our biscuit lines hard here, echoing Hershey's warnings, but we've mitigated via palm oil alternatives and localized sourcing from Ghanaian cooperatives under our Sustainable Origins program.

Unfavorables totaled -190 basis points: input inflation at -110 bps (commodities up 8% overall, led by dairy +12% on U.S. feed costs), freight and logistics at -40 bps (despite sequential improvement from Red Sea rerouting), and mix/volume dynamics at -40 bps due to EMEA promotions to counter discounters like Aldi.

To build on that, let's drill into the core factors impacting gross margin: commodity costs, pricing, and mix. Overall, our key CPG input basket—spanning edible oils, sweeteners, cocoa, grains, and packaging—rose just 1.2% year-over-year on an organic basis, a sharp deceleration from the 8-10% inflation we saw in FY2023. This moderation reflects some normalization post-Ukraine war disruptions, but we still faced pockets of volatility. Cocoa prices, for instance, surged 28% year-to-date due to poor West African harvests—echoing the supply shocks that hammered peers like Mondelez and Hershey earlier this year. Edible oils, including palm and soybean, were a bright spot, down 4% sequentially thanks to favorable South American yields and Indonesian palm production rebounding. PET resin for our beverage portfolio held flat, but aluminum for cans ticked up 3% amid energy cost passthroughs in Europe.

Our mitigation here was multifaceted. We entered the quarter with 75% of our cocoa exposure hedged through calendar year 2025 at an average cost 15% below spot, locking in savings of about $45 million. Our enterprise-wide Supply Chain Resiliency Program—now in Phase 3—delivered $120 million in year-to-date productivity, including value engineering on packaging that shaved 2.5% off corrugate costs without compromising shelf impact. Regionally, North America benefited from localized sourcing, keeping our snack bar commodities 5% below global averages, while in Emerging Markets like Brazil and India, rupee and real depreciation amplified local input relief. Looking forward, we're guiding to mid-single-digit commodity inflation in Q4, but our hedging book and multi-supplier strategies position us to outperform.

On pricing, our proactive approach yielded 3.8% net price realization this quarter—above our 3-4% target and resilient despite consumer trade-down pressures. We rolled out targeted list price increases of 5-7% across 65% of our portfolio, including 6% on our powerhouse snack brands like Crunchy Bites and 4% on household essentials akin to P&G's Tide portfolio. Gross pricing was even stronger at 6.2%, with trade spend optimization holding promotionals to just 2.4% of revenue, down 50 bps YoY. Elasticity remained favorable at -2.1x—better than the -2.5x category average per Nielsen data—validating our 'pricing for value' strategy that pairs increases with innovation like our low-sugar reformulations in beverages.

Regionally, North America drove 4.5% pricing power, fueled by premiumization in health-focused categories, while EMEA lagged at 2.1% due to aggressive discounters like Aldi and Lidl pressuring everyday low-price SKUs. In Asia-Pacific, we captured 5.2% through e-commerce channel pricing premiums on platforms like Tmall. Competitively, this stacks up well against Unilever's reported 2-3% pricing moderation; our data shows we gained 10 bps of market share in core categories. Strategically, we're layering in dynamic pricing tools powered by AI analytics—piloted in 20% of our U.S. distribution—which adjust in real-time based on basket affinity and competitor intel, targeting another 50 bps uplift in FY2025.

Mix was our margin accelerator, contributing a full 140 basis points of expansion. We saw a 3.2-point shift toward higher-margin premium and RGM—return on gross margin—segments, including a 12% volume pivot from value multipacks to our 'Indulge' line of organic snacks and plant-based household cleaners. Premium beverages, like our new electrolyte-infused waters competing with Prime and Gatorade, grew 18% and carry 55% gross margins versus 38% for legacy carbonated soft drinks. This reflects our portfolio optimization playbook: pruning low-RGM 'tail' SKUs (now <5% of revenue, down from 12% two years ago) and accelerating innovations with 8-10% margins above category norms.

Geographically, North America's mix shift was strongest at +4.5 points, driven by wellness trends per IRI scan data, while Latin America faced -1 point headwind from economic softness pushing consumers to private label. Our Health and Wellness platform now represents 28% of sales—up from 22% last year—with 52% average gross margins, positioning us for sustained tailwinds as ESG and clean-label demands grow.

These levers—commodity discipline, resilient pricing, and mix optimization—delivered 48.2% gross margins, our highest in five years, and give us conviction in 48.5-49.0% for Q4, with 100 basis points from continued pricing normalization—targeting low-single-digit increases selectively—and another 75 basis points from productivity, including the rollout of AI-driven demand forecasting across our 25 global DCs to reduce inventory obsolescence by 20%. Full-year, we're raising our gross margin outlook to +210 basis points, implying 48.3% for FY2024. Risks remain around commodity volatility—our Q4 cocoa exposure is hedged 85%—and potential U.S. tariff hikes on Mexican imports, which could add 20 bps pressure if enacted.

This margin trajectory underscores our "CPG 2.0" strategy: leveraging data analytics for dynamic pricing, sustainable supply chains for cost resilience, and portfolio shaping toward high-margin adjacencies like plant-based snacks, where we're targeting 25% of sales by 2026.

Next, I'll turn to our market share performance, which continues to underscore the strength of our portfolio and the effectiveness of our growth strategies across categories and regions. As you know, we track market share primarily through IRI and Nielsen syndicated data, focusing on dollar and unit share in measured channels, including grocery, mass, club, and drug, with ACV—All Commodity Volume—distribution as a key leading indicator. Overall, we gained 60 basis points in dollar share globally year-over-year, marking our third consecutive quarter of share expansion, driven by a mix of volume-led growth, targeted pricing actions, and distribution gains totaling 1.2 points in weighted distribution.

Breaking this down first by category, then layering in regional insights, with some color on the initiatives fueling these trends.

Beauty and Personal Care (26% of our portfolio) delivered our strongest share performance, up 120 basis points in dollar share to 14.8% globally. In North America, we expanded to 18.2% share, outpacing category leader Procter & Gamble by 30 bps, thanks to our "Radiant Glow" skincare line, which captured 2.5 share points in facial moisturizers amid surging demand for clean beauty formulations—up 15% category growth per IRI. Premiumization is key here: our higher-margin prestige offerings grew 22% versus flat mass-market declines. In Europe, we held flat at 12.5% amid soft category volumes down 3% due to inflation fatigue, but we gained 80 bps in the UK through sustainable packaging innovations on our "EcoShine" shampoos, aligning with EU green claims regulations. Asia-Pacific was the standout, with 150 bps gains to 11.1% share, led by Indonesia and India where our affordable sachet packs drove 4x volume growth in hair care, countering Unilever's dominance.

Household Care (32% of portfolio) dollar share rose 40 bps to 16.3% globally, resilient despite a 2% category contraction from inventory destocking. Laundry detergents were the engine, up 90 bps in NA to 21.4% share—beating Tide head-on with our enzyme-boosted "PowerClean" pods, which added 1.1 points via e-commerce velocity, now 28% of category sales per NIQ data. We saw distribution gains of 2.3 ACV points here from retailer expansions at Walmart and Kroger. In Latin America, we lost 20 bps to 13.7% amid aggressive pricing from local players like Souza Cruz, but our bleach sub-line stabilized with a 5% volume rebound tied to back-to-school campaigns. EMEA held steady at 15.2%, bolstered by our water-saving fabric softeners, which resonated in water-stressed markets like Spain.

Food and Beverages (24% of portfolio) was a mixed bag here, with flat global dollar share at 12.1%, but underlying volume share up 30 bps excluding transitory pricing gaps. Snacks grew 70 bps to 10.8% in NA, fueled by our "NutriCrunch" protein bars—now #2 behind Kind—capturing 1.4 points in the better-for-you segment amid 12% category expansion. Beverages lagged, down 50 bps to 14.2% globally due to PepsiCo's zero-sugar ramp-up, but we countered with RTD coffee innovations, gaining 2.2 points in Europe where Nespresso faces pod recycling scrutiny. In APAC, beverages shone with 110 bps gains to 9.5% share in China, leveraging ready-to-drink tea formats that tapped into the 18% growth in non-alcoholic functionals.

Health and Wellness (18% of portfolio) share expanded 80 bps to 13.6% globally, our fastest-growing category at +8% organic sales. Oral care led with 140 bps gains in NA to 19.7%, eclipsing Colgate via our hydroxyapatite toothpaste tech in "SmileGuard," which drove 3x trial per Kantar data. Vitamins and supplements added 60 bps in Europe, up to 11.4%, through omnichannel D2C integration with Amazon and Boots. Challenges persist in LATAM, where we shed 30 bps to 10.2% from grey-market imports, but our probiotic yogurts stabilized via localized formulations.

On the regional deep dive: North America (45% of sales): +90 bps to 17.5% aggregate share. Brick-and-mortar velocity up 4%, e-commerce now 22% of our mix versus 15% industry average, per Edge by Ascential. Key: Targeted trade spend optimization yielded 1.5 ACV gains at dollar stores like Dollar General. Europe (25% of sales): +20 bps to 14.2%. Inflation cooled to 2%, but private label pressure bit 1 point; we offset with 300 bps shelf-set wins on eco-credentials. Asia-Pacific (18% of sales): +130 bps to 11.8%, fastest growth at +11% volumes. China MT channel up 25%, India rural expansion via Project Shakti-like micro-entrepreneur networks. Latin America and Rest of World (12% of sales): Flat at 12.9%. Brazil currency headwinds offset Mexico gains from nearshoring supply chains.

Strategically, these trends reflect our "Win with Precision" playbook: 15% of R&D spend on AI-driven consumer insights for faster innovation cycles—e.g., our "FlavorForge" platform accelerated snack launches by 40%. We're pruning low-share SKUs (exit 8% of portfolio), doubling down on megabrands (80/20 rule delivering 65% of growth), and pursuing bolt-on M&A like our recent $250M acquisition of a Korean K-beauty startup. Looking forward, we expect 50-70 bps share gains in FY24, prioritizing premium shelves and sustainability—our 50% recycled plastic goal by 2025 is already winning loyalty, with +5 NPS uplift.

To wrap up pricing's role more specifically, we executed targeted pricing actions averaging +5.2% year-over-year across our portfolio, a slight moderation from the +7.1% in Q2 as we lap tougher comps and respond to moderating inflation. This was achieved through a mix of list price increases on 68% of our SKUs—primarily in Snacks and Confectionery (up 6.8%) and Household Essentials (up 5.9%)—coupled with optimized trade spend, which we reduced by 120 basis points as a percentage of revenue. Importantly, we maintained our high-low pricing model in North America while leaning into everyday low pricing, or EDLP, for high-velocity items like our flagship 'PureRefresh' bottled water line to combat private label aggression from players like Walmart's Great Value.

The impact on sales was clear and positive: pricing and mix contributed +4.8 percentage points to our overall NRG of +3.1%, more than offsetting a modest organic volume decline of -1.7%. Price elasticity remained favorable at approximately -0.35 across the board—meaning for every 1% price hike, volumes dipped just 0.35%—thanks to our premiumization efforts and strong brand equity. This is outperforming category averages; for context, Nielsen data shows CPG elasticity averaging -0.5 in developed markets this quarter. Our average selling price, or ASP, rose 5.4%, driven by a 2.2-point favorable mix shift toward higher-margin premium products like our 'NutriBoost' protein snacks, which grew 14% in dollar sales despite a 3% volume dip.

Breaking it down regionally: North America (52% of sales): Pricing up +4.8%, delivering flat volumes and +2.6% NRG. Here, we faced intense competitive intensity from the duopoly of Kroger and Albertsons, plus Amazon's push into grocery. Our key action was a 5-7% list price increase on fabric care leaders like 'SparkleClean' detergent, which captured 1.2 points of ACV share. Trade promotion effectiveness improved 15% via AI-driven tools from our partnership with NielsenIQ, allowing us to shift from deep discounts to targeted 'price-pack architecture'—e.g., bundling 50oz bottles with coupons—which minimized cannibalization and lifted household penetration by 80 basis points.

EMEA (22% of sales): Strongest pricing at +6.2%, fueling +4.1% NRG despite -1.8% volumes. Inflation-weary consumers in the UK and Germany traded down to discounters like Aldi and Lidl, but our focus on 'value engineering'—reformulating mid-tier 'FreshGlow' skincare without compromising efficacy—held elasticity at -0.28. Premium beauty lines grew 11% in value, offsetting volume softness in staples.

LATAM (15% of sales): Pricing +7.5% amid 25%+ local inflation in Brazil and Argentina, driving +5.3% NRG with volumes down -3.1%. We accelerated dynamic pricing via our proprietary 'PriceOptix' platform, which uses real-time POS data to adjust list prices weekly on beverages like 'ZestQuench' sodas. This countered gray market leakage and preserved 2.1 points of market share versus peers like Ambev.

APAC (11% of sales): Pricing +4.1%, but volumes expanded +1.4% for +3.9% NRG, led by China and India. Premiumization shone here—our 'EliteHarvest' organic teas gained 18% distribution in e-commerce channels like Tmall, where consumers are willing to pay 20% premiums for health claims amid post-COVID wellness trends.

These actions align with our 'Resilient Growth 2026' playbook. We've invested $45 million in technical initiatives this year, including machine learning models for pocket price waterfall analysis—identifying $220 million in untapped pricing power—and expanded zero-based trade spend budgeting, now covering 85% of our portfolio. This has unlocked 150 basis points of gross margin expansion YTD. Looking forward, we expect Q4 pricing of +4-5%, with elasticity improving to -0.3 as input costs stabilize (e.g., sugar down 8% sequentially). Risks include potential tariff escalations on imports, but our 70/30 local-to-import sourcing mitigates this.

In summary, Q3 underscores Summit CPG's ability to navigate headwinds while executing with precision—organic growth above peers, margin expansion, and share gains across regions. This sets us up for full-year organic sales growth of 4-5%, adjusted EPS of $6.45-$6.55, and confidence in our mid-teens ROIC trajectory.

Next, I will turn the call over to Sara to discuss marketing and brand performance.

Sara Lee:
Thank you, Chris. We saw strong performance in our core brands, particularly GlowEssence and NutriBoost. Our digital marketing efforts are driving significant engagement, and we are seeing strong results from our Refresh Revolution campaign. As we dive into our Q3 results, I want to spend some time on marketing campaign effectiveness, which was a key driver behind our 8% year-over-year organic revenue growth and 12% expansion in adjusted EBITDA margins. In the CPG space, where category growth is muted at around 2-3% globally per Nielsen data, our ability to deliver consistent, measurable returns from marketing underscores our competitive edge against peers like Procter & Gamble and Unilever. We achieved an overall marketing ROI of 4.8x this quarter—up from 4.2x in Q2—meaning every dollar invested generated $4.80 in incremental revenue. This was fueled by a smarter mix of omnichannel activations, advanced attribution modeling, and a 25% shift toward high-ROI digital channels.

Our flagship "Refresh Revolution" campaign for our core Refresh Beverages portfolio—think low-sugar sparkling waters and functional energy drinks akin to Celsius or Prime—delivered standout results. Launched in mid-Q2 across TV, CTV, social, and retail media networks like Amazon DSP and Walmart Connect, it drove a 17% sales uplift in tracked households, per IRI scan data, and captured 1.4 points of market share in the $25B U.S. non-alcoholic beverage category. ROAS hit 7.2x overall, with digital components at 9.5x versus 3.1x for linear TV. We saw AOV rise 11% to $18.50 on e-commerce, thanks to bundled promotions and personalized upsell algorithms.

Technically, this success hinged on our enhanced Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) integrated with incrementality testing via geo-holdout experiments. Partnering with platforms like Measured and Nielsen, we isolated causal impact, revealing that 62% of our media lift came from connected TV and YouTube pre-rolls, where view-through conversions were 2.3x higher than benchmarks. We also rolled out AI-driven personalization at scale using our first-party data lake—built on Snowflake and compliant with post-iOS 14.5 privacy standards—which boosted email open rates to 28% (versus industry 21%) and conversion rates by 14% through dynamic content like regional flavor recommendations.

Regionally, performance varied but trended positive. In North America, which accounted for 45% of our media spend, ROAS was 6.1x, propelled by our "Snack Smart" campaign for our HealthCrunch nut bars, mirroring KIND's playbook. TikTok influencer partnerships with micro-creators (10k-50k followers) generated 22% higher engagement than macro-influencers, driving 3.2 million UGC posts and a 9% trial rate among Gen Z. EMEA saw 4.9x ROI, with sustainability messaging resonating—our "EcoPack" initiative for household cleaners lifted sales 13% in the UK and Germany, where EU Green Deal regulations are accelerating premiumization. NielsenIQ data showed us gaining 0.8 share points in a flat €15B European cleaning category.

APAC was our growth engine at 5.7x ROAS, led by live-commerce activations on platforms like Shopee and Lazada in Southeast Asia. Our BeautyGlow skincare line—positioned against L'Oréal's Garnier—achieved 25% sales growth in Indonesia and India via KOL-driven streams, with EPC 18% above targets at $0.42. Challenges persisted in LATAM, where inflation-hit markets like Brazil tempered ROI to 3.8x; here, we pivoted to trade promotions and hyper-local WhatsApp campaigns, stabilizing volume decline to just -1% versus category -4%.

Strategically, these results validate our "Precision Growth" framework: reallocating 35% of budget from traditional to performance media, prioritizing zero-party data collection via loyalty apps (now at 45 million members, up 18% YoY), and doubling down on shoppable social formats. CLV for acquired customers from digital campaigns rose 22% to $156, outpacing CAC of $28. Looking ahead, we're testing generative AI for creative optimization—early pilots show 30% faster production cycles and 15% ROAS uplift—and expanding retail media to 20% of spend, targeting networks like Kroger Precision Marketing.

In summary, our marketing engine is firing on all cylinders, delivering not just efficiency but category leadership in an inflationary, fragmented CPG landscape. We're confident this momentum positions us to hit our full-year ROI target of 4.6x and sustain market share gains.

Following me, Mike Chen will provide an update on our supply chain initiatives.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Sara. We continue to focus on optimizing our supply chain to improve efficiency and reduce costs. We are implementing new technologies and processes to enhance our responsiveness to changing market conditions. We are also actively working to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions.

Drawing from our broader efforts, the "Margin Accelerator Program" and "CPG Lean 2.0" have been pivotal, delivering over $600 million in cumulative COGS savings through zero-based budgeting, procurement optimization, manufacturing efficiencies, and automated lines that cut labor and scrap by 15%. Our Global Supply Chain Resilience Hub, with its digital twin and machine learning, predicted and averted disruptions like Red Sea delays, saving $120 million in Q3 alone. Inventory optimization to 7.2 weeks, hedging 75-85% of key commodities like cocoa and palm oil, and localized sourcing from programs like Sustainable Origins in Ghana have shielded us from volatility in energy, freight, and inputs.

On sustainability, we're advancing toward net-zero by 2030 with Scope 1 and 2 emissions down 22%, 60% recyclable packaging, 50% recycled plastic goal by 2025, and 35% reduction in virgin plastic in EMEA—driving +5 NPS and loyalty while aligning with EU directives. These initiatives not only cut costs but enhance resilience, supporting our premium portfolio shift and high-ROIC growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking a question will be repeated. Our first question comes from Sarah Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Johnson:
Could you provide more insight into the geographic performance, particularly in emerging markets?

Jamie Thompson:
Thanks, Sarah. Absolutely, emerging markets remain a bright spot. In Asia-Pacific, we saw 6.9% organic growth, with standout double-digit gains in Indonesia and India from sachet packs and urbanization trends, gaining 130 bps share to 11.8%. China MT channels grew 25%, and our K-beauty acquisition bolsters this. Latin America grew 4.3% despite currencies, with Mexico nearshoring and Brazil inflation offset by 7.5% pricing.
